Subject: Guarded deployment discovery — networking & residency recap

Thanks for the time earlier, Alex and Kavita — appreciate the clear framing. Quick recap from my side plus proposed next steps so we keep momentum. Please correct anything I mis-stated.

Key pain & goals you emphasized
- Data residency requirement: primary patient records must remain in US-owned VPC; backups can live in our EU region only after explicit approval.
- Regulatory driver: WellPath is pursuing a FedRAMP-equivalent posture for certain modules; procurement requires evidence of data flow and isolation controls.
- Air-gap consideration: for a subset (PHI audit logs + model inputs) you asked whether an air-gapped ingest path is feasible for future phases.
- Latency requirement: 150–250ms median inference for triage workflows (100 tokens), 95th <= 500ms.

Technical constraints noted
- Customer-managed VPC with dedicated peering (no VPN tunnels preferred).
- No public egress of raw logs; we can accept aggregated telemetry via encrypted push (allowed endpoint list).
- On-prem appliance: possible, but procurement prefers VPC-first to avoid hardware procurement cycle.

Proposed next steps (owners & timing)
1) Mutual action plan (MAP) draft — I’ll send the first pass by EOD Monday (attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx). Owner: Soojin.
2) Network sketch + minimal firewall requirements — Ben to outline required ports and peering options by Wed. Owner: Ben Carter.
3) Security artifacts: SOC2 extract + diagram for procurement — attaching Redwood snapshot (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). Owner: Soojin.
4) Procurement kickoff: Kavita to share procurement POC and timeline; WellPath to confirm procurement contact (procurement@wellpathhealth.com).

Attachments I’m sending in this thread:
- wellpath-network-sketch.pdf (initial sketch we discussed)
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary highlights & where to find full report)
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (work-in-progress)

Open questions
- Which submodule(s) require the air-gap option now vs later? You mentioned "audit/archival only" but we should confirm scope.
- Can you confirm whether backups to EU require an encryption-at-rest key managed by WellPath KMS, or would Redwood-hosted KMS be acceptable under contract terms?

Immediate ask
- Alex/Kavita: please confirm procurement POC and whether Peering (AWS VPC Peering) is acceptable. If not, we’ll propose AWS PrivateLink or Transit Gateway alternatives.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with the MAP + a concise firewall port list.

—

Thanks, Soojin — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Air-gap scope: for Phase 1 we only need air-gap for audit logs and raw PHI dumps used for compliance investigations. Triage inference (real-time) must stay low-latency and in our US VPC. Phase 2 might expand.
- EU backups: we require BYOK (bring your own key) for anything replicated to EU. That means WellPath KMS managed keys.

Procurement POC: forwarding the procurement alias (procurement@wellpathhealth.com) — Kavita is looped for timeline. Our target is to have an internal sign-off by 2027-01-15 if possible.

Can Ben or Neha confirm whether Redwood can support KMS key wrapping for EU replicas (i.e., we store encrypted blobs but the KMS policy is controlled by WellPath)? Also, do you have a recommended pattern for the air-gapped ingest (S3 import via removable media or controlled SFTP pickup?)

Appreciate the MAP — looks like the right next artifact.

Quick technical note on the KMS + air-gap questions below. High level: yes, we can support BYOK for EU replicas and a constrained air-gap ingestion path. Details: 

- BYOK for EU replicas: Redwood can accept encrypted blobs where you control the KMS key. Pattern we recommend: encrypt at the application layer with your KMS (envelope encryption) before we store replicas; we do not hold plaintext or key material. We will include contractual controls in the MAP.

- Air-gapped ingest options:
  * Controlled SFTP pickup: WellPath drops encrypted bundles to a customer-managed SFTP host in your VPC; Redwood runs an agent that pulls and ingests into the isolated bucket. Minimal ops but requires an inbound from our agent (can be done over private peering).
  * Physical media import: S3 import via AWS Snowball-style workflow — higher latency, heavy ops; better for large archival backfills.
  * Isolated API gateway in your VPC: we can deploy a sequenced, private-only gateway with strict allowlist. This keeps latency but increases initial setup.

- Network ports: initial sketch attached (wellpath-network-sketch.pdf). Short summary: allow outbound HTTPS to 52.2.XX.XX/32 over 443 for telemetry push if you choose that route; for peering we need no public egress.

I’ll convert this into a short tech appendix and drop into the MAP draft. Want to sync for a 30-min tech deep-dive this week? Wed 11/31 is tight for me — available Thu 12/2 09:00–10:30 PT or Fri 12/3 13:00–15:00 PT.

—Ben
